title: Generic geometric germs detect line-module sections on integral spaces
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a separated algebraic space of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Suppose $X$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible: the rings of affine etale scheme charts are reduced, and the point space in the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] is not a union of two proper closed subsets. Then $|X|$ has a unique generic point $\eta$. Fix any geometric point $\bar\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ above $\eta$, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. The geometric stalk $F=\mathcal O_{X,\bar\eta}$ is a field. For every line module $M$ on the small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space], the geometric stalk $M_{\bar\eta}$ is one-dimensional over $F$, and the germ homomorphism $\Gamma(X,M)\to M_{\bar\eta}$ is injective. A geometric stalk here is the filtered colimit of the sections on pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods of $\bar\eta$, and the germ homomorphism is induced by restrictions. No properness or regularity assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DMZ, lemma-characterize-trivial-pic-integral, first part of proof (generic nonvanishing and field local ring); decent-spaces.tex Tag 0ABV, lemma-decent-generic-points. The generic argument uses only separated finite type and integral, not proper.

proof.text: The diagonal of $X$ is representable by closed immersions by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Each scheme test is a closed immersion, hence proper and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and therefore quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Apply [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] to the nonempty irreducible closed subset $|X|$ itself. It has exactly one generic point $\eta$, so $\overline{\{\eta\}}=|X|$.

source.place: Tags 03JX (lemma-bounded-fibres), 03K6 (proposition-reasonable-sober); scheme closed immersions: morphisms.tex Tag 01W0 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper).

proof.text: Choose a pointed affine etale scheme neighbourhood $(T,\bar t)$ of the fixed $\bar\eta$, using an atlas, an affine open around a lift, and [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift]. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $t$ for the image of $\bar t$. The prime $\mathfrak p$ of $t$ is minimal. Indeed, if $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ is prime, the Zariski closed sets $V(I)$ show that $\mathfrak q\leadsto t$: every $V(I)$ containing $\mathfrak q$ also contains $\mathfrak p$. Continuity in [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-etale-specializations] gives $a(\mathfrak q)\leadsto\eta$. The closure of $\{a(\mathfrak q)\}$ therefore contains $\overline{\{\eta\}}=|X|$, so $a(\mathfrak q)=\eta$ by uniqueness. The same node's no-specializations-in-a-fibre assertion gives $\mathfrak q=t$.

source.place: Tag 0ABV (lemma-decent-generic-points), implication (1) to (2), using Tag 03K5 (lemma-decent-no-specializations-map-to-same-point); geometric lift: spaces-properties.tex Tag 05VN.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is reduced by the hypothesis on affine charts. Hence $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field]. The canonical germ map identifies $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness], $F=\mathcal O_{X,\bar\eta}\cong\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Apply the strict-henselization description [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] to the field $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ at its zero prime, with the separable closure inside $\Omega$ selected by $\bar t$. Its maximal ideal is $0\cdot R^{\mathrm{sh}}=0$, and its residue ring is that separable closure, a field. Thus $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, and hence $F$, is a field. This identifies the geometric stalk with a separable closure of a chart generic field; it does not identify it with all of $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0DMZ (lemma-characterize-trivial-pic-integral), field-local-ring sentence; algebra.tex Tags 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring), 04GP (lemma-strict-henselization)(4),(5), 04GW; spaces-properties.tex Tag 04KF.

proof.text: Take an etale chart trivializing $M$ and lifting $\bar\eta$; such a chart and a lift exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift]. On its localized etale site the trivialization $M\simeq\mathcal O$ and its inverse induce inverse maps on pointed-neighbourhood colimits. These are the original stalks: for every pointed neighbourhood $V$ of $\bar\eta$, its fibre product with the chosen chart, with the pair of lifts, refines $V$ and lies over that chart, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Any two such refinements admit their pointed fibre product as a common refinement. The induced maps are $F$-linear because the trivialization commutes with the local structure-sheaf actions. Consequently $M_{\bar\eta}\cong F$ as $F$-modules, and it has dimension one.

source.place: Tag 04KF (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), first equality by localization at a pointed chart; line modules: sites-modules.tex Tags 0409 and 0B8Q.

proof.text: Let $s\in\Gamma(X,M)$ have zero germ. Equality with zero in the stipulated filtered colimit means that on some pointed etale scheme neighbourhood $v:V\to X$ one has $s|_V=0$: represent the germ and zero on a common neighbourhood and then equalize their representatives at a later stage. Let $W\subseteq X$ be the open image of $V$, supplied by [lem-a1-etale-scheme-map-open-image]. The map $V\to W$ is surjective etale, so the sheaf axiom gives $s|_W=0$. This statement can be tested on any scheme etale over $W$, where its pullback covering from $V$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The image of the pointed lift shows $\eta\in|W|$; hence $W$ is nonempty and dense in the irreducible point space of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0DMZ (lemma-characterize-trivial-pic-integral), generic nonvanishing argument in contrapositive form; spaces-properties.tex Tag 06NF (lemma-etale-image-open).

proof.text: Choose affine etale charts $a:U\to X$ trivializing $M$, covering the small etale site as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For each such chart put $U_W=U\times_XW$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], this is an open subscheme whose point set is $a^{-1}(|W|)$. It is dense in $U$: every nonempty open $B\subseteq U$ has nonempty open image $a(B)$ in $|X|$, since the point map of $a$ is open. That image meets the dense open $|W|$, so $B$ meets $U_W$. Under the trivialization, $s|_U$ is a regular function $f\in A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and $f|_{U_W}=0$.

source.place: Tag 0DMZ (lemma-characterize-trivial-pic-integral), affine trivializing chart; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H4 and 03IR, pointwise pullback and openness.

proof.text: The basic open $D(f)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] is disjoint from $U_W$, because every germ there is zero. Density of $U_W$ and openness of $D(f)$ imply $D(f)=\varnothing$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], every prime of $A$ therefore contains $f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $f\in\sqrt{(0)}$, so $f^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$. Since the affine chart ring $A$ is reduced, $f=0$. Thus $s$ restricts to zero on every trivializing etale chart, and the sheaf axiom gives $s=0$. The germ homomorphism is additive; applying this zero-kernel argument to $s_1-s_2$ proves injectivity. None of these steps uses properness or regularity.
